label: churn100-s4
summary: The model predicts churn as a sum of parts on the logit scale, passed through a sigmoid. Customer service calls barely move the prediction for customers with few calls, because a gate cancels most of their direct edge; once the gate shuts, each further call adds the full direct effect, so for the typical customer predicted risk stays between 2% and 3% over the first few calls and then climbs to 17% and 41% as calls are added (in Oregon the gate is shut for all 84 customers, 0 of them having it open). Heavy daytime calling, helped by evening calling, opens a hinge: the 393 heaviest day users (9.8% of training customers) churned at 48.9% and get 2.63 on the score from the day-usage parts on average. An international plan raises the score and a voice-mail plan lowers it through direct edges (0.72 and -1.20 per sd); replacing the plan-and-usage direct edges by their mean drops training AUC from 0.898 to 0.625. State and area code add fixed per-state shifts that follow the states' training churn rates (Hawaii's 73 customers get -2.94 on the score and churned at 4.1%), account length adds a small rising slope, and one hidden unit is open for 0 training customers. The annotated network reproduces the original to within 4.4e-16 on every training row.
